name: Surface gravity
question: How hard you'd be pulled down standing on each world. Each gridline step is ten times stronger.

items.name: Ceres
items.fact: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt.

items.name: Pluto
items.fact: On Pluto you could jump about 16 times higher than on Earth.

items.name: Triton
items.fact: Triton orbits Neptune backwards and is slowly spiraling inward.

items.name: Eris
items.fact: The discovery of Eris led to Pluto being reclassified as a dwarf planet.

items.name: Callisto
items.fact: Callisto is one of the most heavily cratered objects in the Solar System.

items.name: Europa
items.fact: Europa likely hides a salty ocean under its ice.

items.name: Titan
items.fact: With low gravity and thick air, a person on Titan could fly by flapping wings.

items.name: Ganymede
items.fact: Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury.

items.name: The Moon
items.fact: Moon gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's.

items.name: Io
items.fact: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: Mercury and Mars have almost the same surface gravity, though Mercury is much smaller.

items.name: Mars
items.fact: On Mars you'd weigh a bit over a third of your Earth weight.

items.name: Venus
items.fact: Venus is almost Earth's twin in size and gravity.

items.name: Earth
items.fact: The standard value of Earth's gravity is 9.80665 m/s².

items.name: Saturn
items.fact: Saturn is less dense than water.

items.name: Neptune
items.fact: Neptune has the fastest winds in the Solar System.

items.name: Jupiter
items.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
